content:
sylvie: Quick idea — build a lightweight 'deploy cookbook' wizard in Slack to assemble a release recipe (preflight checks, change-window, canary %, escape-hatch shortcuts). Prototype next sprint? :seedling:

tanner: love the name. do we want this as a slash command or a modal driven flow? slash for power users, modal for step-by-step?

ji-hoon: both. slash to kick it off, modal for the default guided path. suggest command: `/cookbook start <service> [--dry-run]` and `/cookbook apply <id>` for executing a saved recipe.

maria: +1. main things to capture: target binary/image tag, pinned infra vars, change window, canary split, health-check cmds, quick rollback target. also include a field for release-notes link.

sylvie: rough example recipe we can store as YAML in the repo for repeatable runs:

```
recipe:
  service: inference-api
  image: redwood/inference:2026-04-01-1345
  version_label: v1.3.4
  change_window: 2026-04-10T20:00Z/2026-04-10T22:00Z
  canary: 5%
  checks:
    - smoke
    - latency: p95 < 200ms
    - exports-healthy
  rollback_target: v1.3.3
  notes: https://docs.internal/releases/inference-1.3.4
```

devex: UI notes — modal should surface quick 'escape hatch' buttons: `rollback`, `pause-traffic`, `route-to-fallback`. We can wire buttons to pre-authorized endpoints so ops can act from Slack fast.

ops-bot: preflight CI: ✅  build  / ✅  unit tests / ⚠️  perf-smoke flaky (2/3) — recommend gating canary at 2% until perf-smoke stabilizes.

ji-hoon: good catch. cookbook should have an automated suggestion step that reads last N perf-smoke runs and recommends canary percent + warmup delay. pseudocode: `suggest_canary(service) -> {percent: 2, warmup: 3m}`

tanner: permission model — only people in `release` role can `apply`. others can `draft` and `request-approval`. integrate with existing IAM. also log every `apply` as auditable event in S3 + console.

maria: for rollback quickers, add shorthand commands that map to route manipulations: `/cookbook escape <service> --to v1.3.3 --reason "perf regression"` which triggers a scoped runbook, annotated in the release notes.

sylvie: implementation plan (tiny MR):
- /cookbook start modal (devex)
- save recipe as `deploy-cookbook/*.yml` (ops)
- suggestion engine: small lambda reading perf metrics (ji-hoon)
- Slack buttons -> backend API -> infra orchestrator (tanner)

devex: i can prototype modal + buttons this week. will mock the suggestion engine with a static response.

ji-hoon: i'll put together a tiny suggester script and a pytest for edge cases.

tanner: i'll scope RBAC and the audit log. we should reuse `release-guard` roles.

maria: i'll draft 2 cookbook templates for inference-api and embed-service. keep them simple.

sylvie: sweet. can we aim to have a demo in next week's eng-releases meeting? if yes, assign owners in the sprint ticket. also naming: prefer `/cookbook` over `/deploy-wizard` to keep it friendly.

ops-bot: action logged: ticket #INF-587 created (owners: devex, ji-hoon, tanner, maria).

sylvie: thanks all. if anyone thinks of required safety checks we missed (e.g., KMS key rotation window, DB migration locks), flag here. otherwise i'll draft the RFC and link in the ticket. :sparkles:
